name: Funded degree prompt guide
description: The funded degree prompt from the reel: tell Claude what you studied and it searches official university pages for PhD and master's programmes that pay your fees and a living stipend, then matches a professor and drafts your first email.

page.title: Find a PhD or master's that pays you
page.sub: One free prompt from the reel. Some universities cover your fees and pay you to live while you study. Claude searches the official pages, lists what each programme pays, who can apply and the deadline, then picks a professor whose work matches yours and drafts a first email about one of their real papers.
page.prompt_how: Paste this into a Claude chat with web search switched on (the free plan has it). Change the parts in square brackets first.
page.prompt_note: Deadlines for most programmes fall between November and January.
page.tested_title: We ran it ourselves, for a PhD in AI

results.name: It read 20 official pages and listed 8 funded programmes

page.tested_text: We ran it in a normal Claude chat as someone with a bachelor's in computer science who wants a PhD in AI. It read **20 official pages** and listed **8 funded programmes**, with what each one states it pays, whether international students can get it, and the deadline. **Two deadlines were 8 days away.** We then checked two figures ourselves on the universities' own pages: the University of Toronto's package for international PhD students admitted in 2026-27 is **$41,122 (Canadian dollars)** with funding guaranteed for 60 months for direct entry, and UBC's is **$46,236**. For the best three it named a professor, one real recent paper and a first email under 120 words. **Not checked:** whether those professors are taking students. Claude said so itself. Nothing here promises a place: Toronto says only 5 to 10% of applicants get an offer.
page.tip: **The tip:** fill in the bracket in the email with one true sentence about your own project. A professor can tell a template from a real note.

prompt:
You are my funded-degree finder. About me: I have [your degree and subject], I want [a PhD / a master's] in [your field], I can study in [countries], and I cannot pay tuition fees.

Search the web right now for programmes that are fully funded: tuition paid AND a living stipend or salary. Use official university and funder pages only. For each one give me: the university and programme, the country, what the funding covers and the yearly stipend or salary as the page states it, whether international students can get it, the next application deadline, and the link to the official page.

Then pick the three that fit me best and for each one name one real professor or lab there whose recent work matches my interest, with the link to their page, and write a short first email to that professor (under 120 words) that mentions one specific paper or project of theirs.

Rules: only programmes and people you actually found, each with its link. Never invent a stipend, a deadline or a name. If a page does not state something, write 'not stated'. Give me the 8 best in a table, ordered by deadline. Finish with the three things that most often get an application rejected.

followups.label: Am I eligible?
followups.prompt: For the three best, list every entry requirement on the official page (degree, grades, English test, references) and tell me which ones I meet, given this: [your grades, tests and experience].
followups.note: Check before you spend a week on an application.

followups.label: A statement of purpose
followups.prompt: Using the programme page for [programme], give me an outline for my statement of purpose: what each paragraph must show, and the three mistakes to avoid. Don't write it for me.
followups.note: It has to be yours, or it reads like everyone else's.

followups.label: Scholarships as well
followups.prompt: Now search for scholarships I could add on top, for [my nationality] students in [field], with the amount, the deadline and the official link.
followups.note: Some stack with a funded place.

checklist.detail: One professor at a time, from your own email.

safety: **Nothing here promises a place.** These programmes are competitive: one of the pages we read says 5 to 10% of applicants get an offer.
**Check every figure on the official page.** Stipends, rules and deadlines change each year, and some apply only to home or only to international students.
**Write to professors as yourself.** Read their paper first. Don't send the same email to twenty people.
